title: Taiwanese Shoppers Grow Cautious Even as the Economy Booms
summaryZh: AI推高零件價格，台灣消費者信心十月下跌，耐久財購買意願創2009年來新低。
summaryHi: AI से पुर्ज़े महँगे हुए; अक्टूबर में ताइवान का उपभोक्ता विश्वास गिरा, टिकाऊ सामान ख़रीदने की इच्छा 2009 के बाद सबसे कम।
summaryEs: La IA encarece componentes: la confianza del consumidor en Taiwán cae en octubre y la compra de bienes duraderos toca mínimos desde 2009.
summaryJa: AI需要で部品が値上がりし、台湾の10月の消費者信頼感が低下。耐久財の購入意欲は2009年以来の低水準に。
summaryKo: AI로 부품값이 오르며 대만 10월 소비자 신뢰지수 하락, 내구재 구매 의향은 2009년 이후 최저.
summaryEn: Taiwan's consumer confidence fell in October as AI-driven price rises hit spending plans, with big-ticket buying at a 2009 low.
paragraphs: Taiwan's economy may be booming on the back of the artificial intelligence trade, but its consumers are in a gloomier mood. National Central University's consumer confidence index slipped 2.5 points in October to 66.27, according to figures released on Tuesday.

The survey, conducted from October 18 to 21 with 3,162 adults, measures how people feel about the next six months in six areas. Three of them fell, and the steepest decline came in willingness to buy durable goods such as cars and appliances. That subindex dropped to 82.97, its lowest reading since September 2009.

Wu Dachrahn, who directs the university's research centre on Taiwan's economy, blamed knock-on inflation. Global demand for AI hardware has pushed up the price of electronic components, he explained, and those costs are being passed on to everyday products.

Views of the local economy and household finances also weakened, while a separate home-buying index fell 8.2 points to 90.64. Wu said confidence in the property market remained fragile despite the central bank easing lending rules in September. By contrast, the employment subindex rose to a two-year high.

The government forecasts growth of 11.05 percent for 2026. Even so, Wu urged consumers to keep an eye on risks from the AI cycle and from US and Chinese tariff policies, which could weigh on Taiwan's exports.
Many people in Taiwan feel less happy about spending money. A university asks shoppers every month how they feel. In October, its number went down by 2.5 points to 66.27.
The biggest fall was about buying big things, like cars, fridges and TVs. This number is now at its lowest point since 2009.
Why? Many computer parts are now more expensive. The world wants these parts for AI, so their prices go up. Phones and other home machines cost more too.
There is some good news. More people feel safe about their jobs. This number is at its highest in two years.
The government thinks the economy will grow a lot this year. But an expert says shoppers should watch for problems, like taxes on trade from the US and China.
sentZh: 台灣有很多人對花錢感到比較不開心。
有一所大學每個月都會詢問購物者的感受。
十月，它的數字下降了2.5點，來到66.27。
跌最多的是購買大型物品，例如汽車、冰箱和電視。
這個數字現在是2009年以來的最低點。
為什麼？
現在很多電腦零件變得更貴了。
全世界都想要這些零件來做人工智慧，所以價格上漲。
手機和其他家用機器也變貴了。
也有一些好消息。
更多人對自己的工作感到安心。
這個數字是兩年來最高。
政府認為今年經濟會大幅成長。
但一位專家說，購物者應該注意一些問題，例如美國和中國對貿易課的稅。

paragraphs: Taiwanese consumers are feeling less confident, even though the economy is growing fast. A monthly survey by National Central University found that its consumer confidence index fell 2.5 points in October to 66.27.

The survey asked more than 3,000 adults about six areas, including prices, jobs, the stock market and their family finances. The sharpest drop was in plans to buy expensive goods such as cars and home appliances. That number fell to 82.97, its lowest level since September 2009.

According to Wu Dachrahn, an economist at the university, the global boom in artificial intelligence is part of the reason. Demand for electronic parts has jumped, so many products that use them now cost more.
Not all the news was bad. Confidence about finding and keeping a job rose to its highest level in two years. Some traditional industries, such as machinery and metals, are also doing better.

The government expects the economy to grow by about 11 percent this year. However, Wu said people still worry about rising prices and the housing market, and he warned that trade taxes from the US and China could hurt exports.
sentZh: 雖然經濟成長快速，台灣消費者卻越來越沒有信心。
國立中央大學的每月調查發現，其消費者信心指數十月下跌2.5點，降至66.27。
這項調查詢問了三千多名成年人對六個方面的看法，包括物價、工作、股市和家庭財務。
下跌最多的是購買汽車、家電等昂貴商品的計畫。
該數字跌至82.97，是2009年9月以來的最低水準。
中央大學經濟學者吳大任表示，全球人工智慧熱潮是原因之一。
電子零件的需求大增，因此許多使用這些零件的產品現在變得更貴。
消息並非全是壞的。
對找到和保住工作的信心升到兩年來最高。
機械和金屬等一些傳統產業的表現也在好轉。
政府預期今年經濟將成長約11%。
不過，吳大任說民眾仍擔心物價上漲和房市，他也警告，美國和中國的貿易稅可能傷害出口。

sentZh: 台灣經濟或許靠著人工智慧貿易而蓬勃發展，但消費者的情緒卻更加低迷。
根據週二公布的數據，國立中央大學的消費者信心指數十月下滑2.5點，降至66.27。

主持該校台灣經濟發展研究中心的吳大任，將原因歸咎於連鎖性的通膨。
他解釋，全球對人工智慧硬體的需求推高了電子零組件的價格，而這些成本正轉嫁到日常產品上。

paragraphs: For an economy forecast to expand by more than 11 percent this year, Taiwan has a surprisingly anxious population of shoppers. National Central University's monthly consumer confidence index retreated 2.5 points in October to 66.27, extending a mood of caution that sits awkwardly alongside the headline growth figures.

Of the survey's six components, the one tracking intentions to buy durable goods suffered the sharpest fall, sinking to 82.97. That is the weakest reading since September 2009, when the island was still recovering from the global financial crisis. Sentiment about the domestic economy dropped 4.33 points, and confidence in family finances slid by 1.76 points.

Wu Dachrahn, director of the university's research centre on economic development, attributed much of the gloom to inflationary spillover from the AI boom. As data centres around the world compete for chips and other components, he argued, prices for the same parts in household electronics have climbed, squeezing ordinary budgets.

Housing adds to the unease. A home-buying index compiled with Taiwan Realty fell 8.2 points to 90.64, and Wu noted that the central bank's decision in mid-September to loosen selective credit controls had done little to restore faith in the property market. The one bright spot was employment, whose subindex reached a two-year high, while traditional sectors such as machinery and base metals showed signs of recovery.

Wu cautioned that the outlook remains exposed to the path of global AI investment and to tariff policies in Washington and Beijing, either of which could dent the export engine on which Taiwan's growth depends.
sentZh: 一個預計今年將成長逾11%的經濟體，購物者卻出人意料地焦慮。
國立中央大學的每月消費者信心指數十月回落2.5點至66.27，延續了一股謹慎氣氛，與亮眼的整體成長數字顯得格格不入。
在調查的六個分項中，追蹤耐久財購買意願的分項跌幅最大，降至82.97。
這是自2009年9月以來最弱的讀數，當時台灣仍在從全球金融危機中復甦。
對國內經濟的看法下跌4.33點，對家庭財務的信心則下滑1.76點。
該校經濟發展研究中心主任吳大任，將這股悲觀情緒大多歸因於人工智慧熱潮外溢的通膨效應。
他認為，隨著全球資料中心競相搶購晶片和其他零組件，家用電子產品中相同零件的價格也跟著上漲，壓縮了一般人的預算。
住房問題更加深了不安。
與台灣房屋合編的購屋指數下跌8.2點至90.64，吳大任指出，央行九月中旬放寬選擇性信用管制的決定，對恢復民眾對房市的信心幫助不大。
唯一的亮點是就業，其分項指數達到兩年新高，而機械、基本金屬等傳統產業也出現復甦跡象。
吳大任提醒，前景仍受全球人工智慧投資走向以及華府和北京關稅政策的影響，兩者都可能削弱台灣賴以成長的出口引擎。

paragraphs: A striking gap has opened between Taiwan's macroeconomic performance and the way its citizens feel about their own prospects. While officials project growth of 11.05 percent for 2026, a survey released on Tuesday by National Central University shows consumer confidence slipping 2.5 points in October to 66.27.

The index, compiled from 3,162 responses gathered between October 18 and 21, assesses expectations over the coming six months across six dimensions. Most notably, willingness to purchase durable goods plummeted to 82.97, a level not seen since September 2009. Perceptions of the domestic economic climate and of household finances also deteriorated.

According to Wu Dachrahn, who heads the university's economic research centre, the explanation lies partly in what economists call knock-on inflation. Soaring global demand for artificial intelligence has driven up the cost of electronic components, and these increases are gradually being transmitted to consumer products. Combined with persistent doubts about the housing market, this has made many households reluctant to commit to major purchases.

Nevertheless, the data are not uniformly negative. The employment subindex rose by one point to 77.7, its highest level in two years, suggesting that the labour market remains robust. Traditional industries, including machinery and base metals, also appear to be regaining momentum.

Wu argued that consumers should remain alert to external risks, particularly the volatility of AI investment and the tariff policies of the United States and China. Taken together, the figures illustrate how rapid growth driven by a single sector does not necessarily translate into widespread economic optimism.
sentZh: 台灣的總體經濟表現與民眾對自身前景的感受之間，出現了明顯的落差。
官方預估2026年成長率為11.05%，但國立中央大學週二公布的調查顯示，消費者信心十月下滑2.5點至66.27。
該指數彙整了10月18日至21日蒐集的3,162份回覆，評估民眾對未來六個月在六個面向的預期。
最值得注意的是，購買耐久財的意願暴跌至82.97，為2009年9月以來未見的水準。
民眾對國內經濟情勢和家庭財務的看法也都惡化。
主持該校經濟研究中心的吳大任表示，部分原因在於經濟學家所說的連鎖性通膨。
全球對人工智慧的需求飆升，推高了電子零組件的成本，而這些漲幅正逐漸轉嫁到消費性產品上。
再加上民眾對房市持續存疑，許多家庭因此不願進行大額消費。
儘管如此，數據並非全都負面。
就業分項指數上升1點至77.7，為兩年來最高，顯示勞動市場依然強健。
機械和基本金屬等傳統產業似乎也正在恢復動能。
吳大任認為，消費者應對外部風險保持警覺，尤其是人工智慧投資的波動以及美國和中國的關稅政策。
綜合來看，這些數據說明了由單一產業帶動的快速成長，不一定會轉化為普遍的經濟樂觀。
